title: Horizon Retail - POC scoping (timeline & milestones)
next_steps: Send POC SOW and pricing by 2025-10-17
Provision test account & generate API keys
Run initial benchmark (traffic profile A) and share results
action_items: Alex Chen: Send SOW and high-level pricing by 2025-10-17
Maya Singh: Provide benchmark config, sample scripts, and expected metrics by 2025-10-16
Priya Kapoor (Horizon): Share sample dataset and access plan by 2025-10-20
Ethan Cole (Horizon): Confirm success criteria (latency/cost/quality) by 2025-10-17
Jordan Lee: Create runbook for access/setup and invite infra contact by 2025-10-15
summary: POC scoping call to align success criteria, sizing, benchmark plan, and timeline for a 6-week POC. Agreed milestones: kickoff (this week), access setup & initial run (week 1), mid-point review with metrics (week 3), exec readout (week 6). Success criteria: p95 latency <200ms for critical endpoints, throughput X qps, cost target <$0.10 per 1k tokens (target), and no PII exfiltration. Next steps: SOW, security pack, test account, and benchmark scripts.
topics: Timeline & milestones (kickoff, access, mid-point, exec readout)
Deployment options: hosted vs dedicated vs private
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Alex Chen from Redwood, AE on the account. We got Maya (SE) and Jordan from solutions here. How's everyone?
[00:12] Ethan Cole: Good, thanks. Ethan here, Head of ML at Horizon. We've got Priya and Liam as well.
[00:20] Alex Chen: Great. Goal for today is to scope the POC timeline and milestones, align on success criteria, get sizing and benchmark approach. We want to leave with clear next steps.
[00:30] Maya Singh: quick note, transcription might mess up product names, so Redwood Dedicated may come out weird in the notes, sorry in advance.
[00:36] Priya Kapoor: that's fine.
[00:38] Liam O'Sullivan: We're mainly evaluating serving economics and latency on our recommendation engine traffic. Also security stack — we can't send data off-prem without review.
[00:46] Alex Chen: understood. Ethan, can you give a quick summary of the workload and what success looks like?
[00:52] Ethan Cole: Sure. We have a recommendations model that powers product recs on web and mobile. Peak traffic is roughly 120 qps, 95th is ~90 qps. Typical request size is 256 tokens input, responses ~64 tokens. Success criteria: p95 latency under 200 milliseconds for the hot path, maintain similar ranking quality to our baseline model (we'll provide evals), and ideally cost per 1k tokens below $0.10 — that's a target not hard requirement. Also key: audit logs, RBAC, and KMS integration.
[01:25] Maya Singh: sounds reasonable; for the POC we'll mirror your traffic profile — we usually run synthetic traffic with your sample dataset to measure p50/p95 and throughput. We'll also run a quality regression on your test set.
[01:36] Priya Kapoor: For access — we'll need to provision a VPC peering or IP allowlist depending on the deployment. Which approach do you recommend?
[01:44] Jordan Lee: For an initial POC most customers opt for hosted API with a VPC egress or IP allowlist to simplify setup. If you need dedicated hardware or on-prem later we can pivot — but that adds setup time.
[01:58] Liam O'Sullivan: Latency is crucial so if hosted adds 30-50ms that's significant. Can you show us expected numbers?
[02:05] Maya Singh: We'll include a latency breakdown in the benchmark — network + model inference. For hosted API we typically see p95 60-120ms for similar workloads on our curated open models; dedicated can shave off another 20-40ms depending on GPU and quantization. There's variance though.
[02:25] Ethan Cole: What about model variants — we want to try 2 sizes: a smaller quantized variant for cost and a larger for quality.
[02:32] Alex Chen: yes, plan is two arms: cost-optimized (quantized, batching) and quality arm (full precision). We'll route the benchmark accordingly.
[02:40] Priya Kapoor: Security questions: SOC2 reports, KMS/HSM integration, and audit logs — can you share docs?
[02:46] Jordan Lee: We'll share the security pack — SOC2, ISO, sample audit logs, pen test summary, and details about our KMS integrations. Expect a link.
[02:54] Ethan Cole: timeline? We have a holiday freeze in mid-November so want to finish exec readout by 2025-11-20.
[03:02] Alex Chen: Ok working backward: if exec readout is week of 2025-11-17, POC needs to be ~6 weeks. Proposed milestones: kickoff this week (Week 0), access setup & initial runs (Week 1), full benchmark and mid-point review (end of Week 3), stabilization and final runs (Week 5), exec readout and handoff (Week 6).
[03:24] Maya Singh: We'll aim to get baseline runs in Week 1 to identify perf regressions. Mid-point will focus on performance, cost, and quality metrics.
[03:33] Priya Kapoor: Who will need access from our side? Network, sample dataset, and a point of contact for infra.
[03:38] Ethan Cole: Priya will own infra access, I'll handle evaluation & metrics. Liam will be present at the exec readout.
[03:45] Alex Chen: Perfect. On benchmarks — we'll run three scenarios: A) production-sim traffic (peak bursts), B) steady-state high throughput for throughput numbers, and C) cold-start latency for short sessions. Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, cost per 1k tokens, and model quality delta on your eval set.
[04:07] Maya Singh: We'll include KV cache warm-up and batching configs; those can change effective latency. We'll share tuning knobs.
[04:14] Priya Kapoor: Do you support rolling canary or A/B during POC? We might want a canary to test real traffic on a small percentage.
[04:21] Jordan Lee: Yes, Redwood supports canary rollouts, A/B tests and fallback policies. For safety we can run synthetic traffic first and then a 1% canary if you want.
[04:31] Liam O'Sullivan: If we do canary we need rate limits and quota enforcement plus logging to our Splunk instance. Can you forward logs?
[04:36] Maya Singh: We can push structured logs and traces. We'll coordinate the log delivery method in the runbook.
[04:40] Ethan Cole: For quality regressions, we'll provide a test suite. What's your criteria for passing?
[04:46] Alex Chen: Agree on a threshold: quality delta (NDCG or similar) within 2% of baseline on your test set. If quality drops more we'll iterate on model variants.
[04:56] Priya Kapoor: For costs, can you give a rough estimate for the POC run? We need a burn budget cap.
[05:02] Jordan Lee: Initial estimate depends on tokens processed during benchmarks; for a standard 6-week POC we usually allocate a $5k-$15k credit depending on throughput. We'll put a target burn and alerting in the SOW.
[05:14] Ethan Cole: That range is fine; please call out the assumptions in the SOW.
[05:18] Alex Chen: We'll do that. Now on setup tasks: Jordan will send a runbook for network and credentials; Maya will drop benchmark scripts and container images; Alex will send SOW and pricing; customer to provide dataset and infra contacts.
[05:35] Priya Kapoor: For access we prefer a minimal network punch: allowlist IP + service account keys. We can do VPC peering if necessary but that'll take longer.
[05:44] Maya Singh: allowlist IP for hosted is fastest; we'll note exact egress ranges. For dedicated/private we can take the VPC route but timeline expands by ~2 weeks.
[05:55] Liam O'Sullivan: Noted. Mid-point review — what do you expect? A deck with metrics and recommendations?
[06:02] Alex Chen: yes mid-point will be a data-driven review: latency/throughput/cost/quality graphs, blockers, and recommended optimizations. We'll propose quantization and batching adjustments for cost arm.
[06:14] Ethan Cole: and final exec readout should include recommended deployment (hosted vs dedicated vs private) and TCO comparison.
[06:20] Jordan Lee: We'll prepare a TCO slide with projected per-1M token costs for each option and expected latency ranges.
[06:27] Priya Kapoor: Any regulatory flags? We need assurance around data residency — our sample data can be anonymized.
[06:33] Maya Singh: We'll support region pinning in Hosted, Dedicated can be in your cloud region, and Private is on-prem. We'll document residency controls in the security pack.
[06:44] Ethan Cole: OK good. Anything else on success criteria?
[06:47] Priya Kapoor: Also monitoring retention—how long do logs persist? We need 90 days for the POC.
[06:52] Jordan Lee: Default retention 30 days, enterprise add-on up to 365 days; for POC we can enable 90-day export to your storage.
[07:00] Alex Chen: Recap and timeline: Kickoff this week (we'll send calendar invite), Jordan sends runbook and security pack by 2025-10-15, Maya sends benchmark scripts by 2025-10-16, Alex sends SOW by 2025-10-17. Customer provides dataset and infra access by 2025-10-20. Mid-point review scheduled end of Week 3 (target 2025-11-03). Exec readout target week of 2025-11-17.
[07:25] Ethan Cole: That works for us.
[07:27] Priya Kapoor: We'll aim to have infra ready by 10/20.
[07:30] Liam O'Sullivan: I'll be at the exec readout.
[07:33] Alex Chen: Great. Any blockers?
[07:35] Ethan Cole: SOC2 docs and KMS details are priority — we need those before access.
[07:40] Jordan Lee: We'll send the security pack link in the next 24 hours.
[07:43] Maya Singh: I'll also include example benchmark outputs so you know what to expect.
[07:47] Alex Chen: OK thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the SOW, security docs, runbook and scripts. Any final Qs?
[07:54] Priya Kapoor: none from me.
[07:55] Ethan Cole: nope.
[07:56] Liam O'Sullivan: thanks.
[07:58] Alex Chen: Thanks all — talk soon.
[08:02] (call ends)
